findings.title: No Organization or WebSite structured data was found anywhere on the site
findings.evidence: 0 of 5 crawled HTML pages contain JSON-LD or microdata of an Organization/LocalBusiness/WebSite type. Types observed across the site: none

suggested_action.summary: Publish one Organization (or LocalBusiness) JSON-LD block site-wide, plus a WebSite block on the homepage.
steps: Add an Organization node with name, url, logo and a description.
Add sameAs links to the official profiles the organization controls.
Include contact details (telephone / email / address) matching the visible contact page.
Serve the block in the initial HTML on every page, or at least on the homepage and about page.

findings.confidence_reason: deterministic rule on measured values; direct DOM/HTTP observation; sample of 5 pages; consistent across 5/5 pages
findings.impact: There is no explicit machine-readable statement of who the site belongs to, so the brand's identity, official name and linked profiles must be inferred from prose - a common cause of entity ambiguity and misattribution.
findings.priority_reason: impact 0.80 (severity high) x reach 1.00 x confidence 0.98 x fixability 0.85

findings.title: Most crawled pages expose no navigation region
findings.evidence: 0 of 5 crawled HTML pages contain a <nav> element or role="navigation"; the homepage exposes 1 internal links in total. Navigation was detected structurally (nav landmark plus internal links inside it), so a visually styled menu that uses neither will also be reported here.

suggested_action.summary: Provide a consistent primary navigation region on every page, marked up as a nav landmark.
steps: Wrap the primary menu in a <nav> element present on every template.
Include links to the main sections (offering, pricing, about, contact).
Make sure the links exist in the server-rendered HTML, not only after client-side hydration.

findings.confidence_reason: deterministic rule on measured values; direct DOM/HTTP observation; sample of 5 pages; consistent across 5/5 pages
findings.impact: Without a consistent navigation region, a visitor who lands on an interior page has no reliable way to move to the rest of the site, so the visit usually ends on the landing page.
findings.priority_reason: impact 0.80 (severity high) x reach 1.00 x confidence 0.98 x fixability 0.60

Add two or three contextual links to closely related pages.

suggested_action.summary: Serve the primary content of these pages in the initial HTML response (server-side rendering, static generation or hydration of pre-rendered markup).
steps: Identify which content blocks are injected client-side on the listed pages.
Render that content server-side (SSR/SSG) or inline it as pre-rendered markup that hydration replaces.
Re-test with JavaScript disabled and confirm the key facts appear in the raw HTML.
Where full SSR is impractical, mirror the key facts in JSON-LD delivered in the initial HTML.

findings.impact: Retrieval clients that do not execute JavaScript see only a fraction of the page, so product, pricing or company facts that live in the rendered DOM may not be extracted at all.

findings.title: Potential freshness risk: the most recent dates on the site are several years old
findings.evidence: 5 of 5 dated pages show no date later than 2025; the newest date found anywhere on the crawled pages is 2016. Dates were read from time elements, article metadata and JSON-LD datePublished/dateModified values. An old date does not prove the content is out of date - it only means nothing on the page signals recency.

suggested_action.summary: Publish explicit last-updated dates and refresh the pages whose facts have changed.
steps: Review the listed pages and correct any facts that have changed.
Add dateModified to the page's structured data when content is revised.
Show a visible 'last updated' date on pages where recency matters.
Avoid auto-bumping dates on unchanged pages - that removes the signal's value.

findings.confidence_reason: deterministic rule on measured values; direct DOM/HTTP observation; sample of 5 pages; consistent across 5/5 pages; conflicting signals present
findings.impact: Without a recent date signal, automated systems have no evidence that the information still holds, so they may prefer more recently dated third-party sources when describing the brand.
findings.priority_reason: impact 0.50 (severity medium) x reach 1.00 x confidence 0.80 x fixability 0.60

technical_details.observation: 5 of 5 dated pages show no date later than 2025; the newest date found anywhere on the crawled pages is 2016.
technical_details.details: Dates were read from time elements, article metadata and JSON-LD datePublished/dateModified values. An old date does not prove the content is out of date - it only means nothing on the page signals recency.

possible_benign_explanations: Reference content that has not changed is correctly left undated; an old date is not evidence that the facts are wrong.

findings.title: No XML sitemap was found
findings.evidence: Neither /sitemap.xml nor any Sitemap: directive in robots.txt returned a usable sitemap. 5 HTML pages were reachable by link following.

suggested_action.summary: Publish an XML sitemap and reference it from robots.txt.
steps: Generate a sitemap listing canonical URLs of the public pages.
Serve it at /sitemap.xml with HTTP 200 and content-type application/xml.
Add a 'Sitemap: https://<host>/sitemap.xml' line to robots.txt.

findings.confidence_reason: deterministic rule on measured values; direct DOM/HTTP observation; sample of 5 pages
findings.impact: Without a sitemap, automated systems must rely entirely on link discovery, so pages that are weakly linked may never be reached.
findings.priority_reason: impact 0.50 (severity medium) x reach 0.50 x confidence 0.90 x fixability 0.90

findings.title: 1 page(s) contain a JSON-LD block that does not parse
findings.evidence: http://demo.example/: JSONDecodeError: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 1 column 59 (char 58) The block is present in the HTML but is not valid JSON, so a consumer must discard it entirely.

suggested_action.summary: Fix the JSON syntax so each ld+json block parses, then validate the vocabulary.
steps: Run each block through a JSON parser and correct the syntax error reported here.
Escape quotes and remove trailing commas in templated values.
Validate the corrected block against schema.org expectations for its @type.

findings.confidence_reason: deterministic rule on measured values; direct DOM/HTTP observation; sample of 5 pages
findings.impact: Structured data that fails to parse provides no machine-readable facts at all, so the effort of publishing it is wasted and the page falls back to text interpretation.
findings.priority_reason: impact 0.50 (severity medium) x reach 0.20 x confidence 0.90 x fixability 0.85
